EA-006.note: Line and Arrow preserve ordered endpoints (direction), optional curved control geometry, border style (solid/dash/dot/dashDot/dashDotDot), thickness, arrow style (classic/modern/double/basic/line), shadow and opacity through bounded XANN read/write (unknown fields kept, older documents load at defaults and re-serialize byte-identically), one shared paintShape path for canvas and export, one-undo-step native edit dialog, session creation defaults, copy/paste/duplicate, move and resize. Decisions: (1) borderStyle, shadow* reuse the EA-005 names, values and defaults, which follow the reference XerahS Annotation.cs/LineAnnotation.cs/BorderStyle.cs; the reference Arrow has no borderStyle, so Arrow also accepts it (dashes the shaft, head stays solid) because EA-006 lists border style for both. (2) Arrow style is persisted as `style` with camelCase values classic/modern/double/basic/line, read case-insensitively, as in reference ArrowAnnotation.cs/ArrowStyle.cs; head geometry and size multipliers (2.0 classic/double, 3.0 modern, 1.75 basic/line, length 3x) follow the reference, so head size is derived from thickness and has no field; Modern is straight and drops the curve, as in the reference CurvedSegmentHelper. (3) The reference stores the curve as `curvePoint` {x,y} in document pixels plus `curvePointActivated` (a point the quadratic passes through at its middle). Here it is the optional third entry of the fractional `points`, so move/resize/flip and the shared all-annotation transform carry it with the endpoints; reference curvePoint/curvePointActivated are accepted on read and converted. Writes use points[2]. Lines or arrows with more than 3 points remain legacy polylines. Curve anchor fractions are bounded to +-1e6. (4) Shadow, ranges and the 1px minimum box follow EA-005. Open: no on-canvas curve drag handle yet (curve is edited in the properties dialog); golden pixels for arrow heads are not contract-defined.

EA-007.note: Freehand stores ordered fractional path points. Canvas and exporter share paintShape with a non-cosmetic round-cap/round-join pen in document units; tests compare coverage at 0.5x/2x/3x and against the export render. The contract requires a documented tolerance without fixing its value; the 0.5 px tolerance, 30 degree corner threshold and 4 px corner reach are the documented Linux values. Cross-platform agreement on these values belongs to parity review, not this implementation status. Simplification is iterative, so long strokes cannot exhaust the stack.

EA-009.note: Step preserves numeric values and existing highest-number allocation. Native selected-number editing is now an owned asynchronous Apply/Cancel dialog over the existing version-1 0..1000000000 range, without clamping stored values to the old UI maximum of 1000000. Shared parsing/create/edit bounds reject invalid numeric values before mutation. Step and Text share document/state/selection/serial/lifetime completion guards. Tests cover zero, one, values above the old UI ceiling and the version-1 maximum; no-op/Cancel, one-step history, undo/redo/reload, stale/disabled/dead owners and deferred-dialog cleanup. Regressions reproduced native clamping and invalid create/edit admission. Alphabetic/Roman mappings and explicit sequence reset need product decisions; start/reset/tail controls, saved preferences and full qualification remain partial. Audit 2026-11-03: Alphabetic (upper/lower), Roman (upper/lower), explicit start number and reset are implemented per the reference XerahS source, which Mike's standing rule makes the tie-breaker where the contract is silent: StepType.cs StepTypeFormatter (alphabetic is bijective base 26: 1=A, 26=Z, 27=AA, case per style; values <= 0 print as plain decimal; Roman is standard subtractive with M repeated above 3999, so 4000=MMMM), MainViewModel.ToolOptions (start number 1..10, default 1, out-of-range clamps) and MainViewModel.RecalculateNumberCounter (next = max(highest+1, start)). Reset retires the Steps that exist so the next allocation is the start number again; existing Steps keep their values and styles; reset and start are editing-session state (no history entry, as in the reference counter) and are not persisted. The style is persisted per object as stepType (reference camelCase names numeric/uppercaseLetter/lowercaseLetter/uppercaseRoman/lowercaseRoman, omitted when numeric, case-insensitive on read, unknown names reject the document) and the ESET-008 StepType preference (PascalCase) is active: stepStyleImplemented accepts the five names, new Steps take the saved style, unknown names stay inert. Native: Drawing Defaults offers the five styles; Edit > Step Start Number... and Reset Step Numbering; the Edit Step dialog changes number and style in one undoable operation; long labels shrink to stay inside the circle. Proving tests: AnnotationShapesTest::stepStylesMapValuesLikeTheReference (0, -5, 1, 4, 9, 26, 27, 52, 702, 703, 1994, 3999, 4000), ::stepStyleNamesFollowTheReferenceSpelling, ::stepStyleRoundTripsPerObjectAndRejectsUnknownNames, ::stepStartAndResetAffectOnlyFutureAllocation, ::stepValuesStayStableAcrossDeleteReorderUndoRedoAndReload, ::stepStyleIsOneUndoableContentEditAndPaintsTheFormattedLabel; EditorCanvasTest::stepCreationUsesSavedStyleStartAndResetAndEditChangesOnlyTheSelectedStep; EditorPreferencesTest::everyReferenceStepStyleIsImplementedAndReachesCreationDefaults; NativeEditorPreferencesTest::missingSavedFontFallsBackWithoutRewritingUntilExplicitReplacement (unknown style stays inert). Remaining gap (an extra beyond the product answers, so the row stays partial): the bullet also requires Step tail state; Step has no tail (reference NumberAnnotation TailPoint/TailPointInitialized/TailEnabled) in the document, renderer or native controls.

EA-011.note: Highlight, Blur, Pixelate, Magnify and Spotlight apply only inside their declared geometry and read only the immutable source image (ShapePainter.cpp effectRegion/paintRegion/paintHighlight/paintMagnify/paintSpotlight; canvas preview and exporter share paintShape). Options follow the reference XANN format (camelCase, defaults omitted on write, unknown fields preserved, bounded validation): `isEllipse` (bool, default false = rectangle) on all five types, Spotlight `blurAmount` (0..1000, default 0) blurring the dimmed area, plus the existing `strength`. Rationale per field: isEllipse = reference BaseEffectAnnotation/SpotlightAnnotation.IsEllipse and ImageEditorOptions.MagnifierEllipse/SpotlightEllipse; blurAmount = reference SpotlightAnnotation.BlurAmount / ImageEditorOptions.SpotlightBlur (reference default 0); Blur has no blur-type option in the reference so none is invented; Highlight/Blur/Pixelate use IsEllipse as in the reference (Highlight has no strength). Persisted strength keeps this build's `strength` name on write. Reference compatibility (read-only aliases, used only when `strength` is absent, consumed so they are not preserved beside `strength`): Blur/Pixelate/Magnify `amount` (0..1000) is read as `strength`, and Spotlight `darkenOpacity` (reference byte 0..255) is read as `strength` percent = darkenOpacity/2.55 (Spotlight strength is the dim percentage, alpha = percent*2.55; 0 maps to 0.01 because strength 0 means the default); out-of-range or non-numeric aliases are rejected like `strength`; an unrelated `amount` on Spotlight/Highlight and an `amount` beside an explicit `strength` stay verbatim. EffectRegionTest::referenceAmountAndDarkenOpacityAreReadAsStrengthAliasesAndWrittenAsStrength covers it. Behaviour changes: Spotlight is now rectangular unless isEllipse is set (reference default; it was always elliptical before), and Magnify no longer draws a stroke border outside its region. A rotated region samples the source under the rotated outline (previously the unrotated box was rotated). Effects replace pixels inside the region from the source, so overlapping effects never see each other's output; Spotlight's dim is an overlay and its blur samples the source. Native: the existing strength dialog gains an Elliptical region checkbox (Highlight: a Rectangle/Ellipse choice) and, for Spotlight, a blur spin box; one Apply is one history operation; unchanged Apply records nothing. Ellipse hit-testing excludes the corners. EffectRegionTest covers rect/ellipse x rotated masks for all five effects, edge clipping incl. 1e9 extents and off-canvas regions, blur position independence, overlap/reorder against the immutable source, repaint independence from canvas contents, canvas==export pixels, byte determinism, XANN round-trip incl. a hand-written reference-style document, invalid option rejection, and native edit/cancel/undo/redo/reload. Independent human visual qualification on target distributions is a release-level activity and is not part of this clause set.
